title: Arkret Account Operation DTOs
description: Closed request and response DTOs for account self-service operations and Account Authority issuer-ledger account-status publication and resolution.

account_subject.description: Deployment-local, non-reversible authentication subject: SHA-256 over utf8('ak.account-subject.v1\n') followed by RFC 8785 JCS of the issuer identity and issuer-local authentication row key. It is confined to the private Account Authority boundary, is always issuer-scoped, and is never an AccountId or resource-owner selector.

dpop_jkt.description: RFC 7638 SHA-256 JWK thumbprint of the holder key, encoded base64url without padding.

status.description: Lifecycle projection only, matching device-lifecycle.md section 14.1. revocation_pending is authority-derived from a durable accepted ak.device.revoke security transaction; trust/evidence quality is reported separately in verification_state.

verification_state.description: Trust verification of the device authorization evidence, separate from lifecycle status. A consumer MUST NOT interpret lifecycle status=active as usable authority unless verification_state=verified.

verification_source.description: Closed provenance of the verification checkpoint behind verification_state, per device-lifecycle.md section 10.1. genesis is the PCR genesis first device, pairing_code an accepted-device pairing or re-verification ceremony, and recovery an accepted recovery unit replacement device. Login factors, SSO sessions, ordinary session grants and bare server projections MUST NOT mint a checkpoint. Required when verification_state is verified, retained when a previously verified checkpoint went stale, and absent when verification_state is unresolved.

revocation_states.description: All gate-relevant durable revoke records for the exact device/generation, sorted by acceptance_seq and Event id. At most 128 distinct unresolved transactions may be admitted; exact replay consumes no slot, a terminal rejected result removes one pending slot, and an already revoked generation accepts no new transaction. Committing one record makes lifecycle status revoked but MUST NOT hide other surviving pending records.

handle_claim_ref.description: Opaque reference to a signed ak.schema.handle_claim.v1 claim, such as an event ref, issuer-local receipt ref, or content-addressed artifact ref.

audience_id.description: Stable target-service authorization identity. A service DID used for signature verification is supplied separately and MUST project to this did_core_id.

expires_at.description: Lease expiry. Issued lifetime MUST be no greater than 15 minutes; 15 minutes is also the v1 default.

account_registration_control_proof.description: Closed control proof for binding an already-published did to principal_id through account register. OIDC, passkey, or agent authentication alone is insufficient to establish DID control. The Account Authority resolves did at high freshness, requires project(did)=principal_id, and selects the current active update key of the entry pinned by did_version_id from verified method history rather than from request-supplied key material. The signature covers every field except signature as canonical JSON with domain separator ak.account_registration_control_proof.v1 and MUST replay the durable challenge issued by ak.gate.account.command.issue_did_binding_challenge.v1.

request_canonical_digest.description: SHA-256 over RFC 8785 JCS of the complete account_register_request_body with proof.request_canonical_digest and proof.signature omitted.

account_subject.description: Service account subject this identity is being bound to. Signed so the proof cannot be replayed to bind the same identity to a different account.

principal_id.description: Stable did_core_id echoed by the challenge and equal to project(did).

did.description: Complete DID resolved by the Account Authority and signed by the holder; it MUST equal the register request did byte-for-byte.

did_version_id.description: Adapter-defined versionId of the entry whose current active update key signed this proof.

control_key_digest.description: SHA-256 over the canonical multikey bytes of the verified current active update key.

dpop_jkt.description: DPoP holder thumbprint echoed by the durable challenge.

expires_at.description: Issued lifetime MUST be no greater than 300 seconds.

verification_method.description: Current active update-key DID URL under did. The verifier parses its bare DID component with the registered adapter and requires the projected did_core_id to equal principal_id; it never appends a fragment to principal_id.

witness_evidence.description: Method-native witness / freshness evidence digest for the external DID, required by deployments that do not host the DID themselves.

account_registration_control_proof.$comment: The method adapter derives the canonical pinned version/entry commitment. control_key_digest serves bounded evidence consumers, and signed method transcript positions are reconstructed from the pinned entry; caller-supplied digest mirrors are rejected.

account_handoff_authentication_proof.description: OIDC authorization-code exchange proof used only to create a DPoP-bound account handoff. The signature is made by the same Ed25519 holder key as the request DPoP proof over utf8('ak.account_handoff_authentication_proof.v1\n') || RFC8785_JCS(this object with signature omitted).

challenge.description: Account Authority-generated challenge persisted with the OIDC authorization transaction and consumed by this exchange.

request_canonical_digest.description: sha256:<lowercase-hex> of SHA-256 over RFC 8785 JCS bytes of the complete account_handoff_request_body with proof.request_canonical_digest and proof.signature omitted.

signature.description: 64-byte Ed25519 signature encoded base64url without padding.

reserved_identity_creation.description: Server-persisted identity-creation checkpoint, readable only by the authenticated current holder of the owning service account's identity-creation lease. It is NOT public: an unfinished reservation would otherwise leak that a specific account is mid-registration, and abandoning it would leave a permanent public trace. Once registration completes the public artifact is the published method-native anchor itself, so this checkpoint never needs to become public. It contains the exact unpublished or already-published registration anchor, never recovery words, seed material, private keys, or an encrypted root export.

registration_anchor_digest.description: sha256:<lowercase-hex> of SHA-256 over RFC 8785 JCS bytes of the complete principal_registration_anchor object.

state.description: Account-Authority-authored durable identity-creation saga state. Clients MUST derive their onboarding phase from this value and MUST NOT infer a phase from local checkpoint presence. reserved_identity MUST be absent only in active and present in every later state.

expires_at.description: Lease expiry. Issued lifetime MUST be no greater than 15 minutes; 15 minutes is also the v1 default.

reserved_identity.description: Holder-authenticated identity-creation checkpoint carried while a reservation exists. It MUST be omitted once the provisional identity has been explicitly abandoned through ak.gate.account.command.abandon_identity_creation.v1: after abandonment the checkpoint MUST NOT remain readable on this or any other holder-readable surface, because leaving it would keep publishing that some account once tried to create an identity. That is a security property, not a cleanup policy.

expires_at.description: Expiry of the conflicting live identity-creation lease. The client uses this authenticated upper bound for waiting UI; it conveys no holder identity or authority.

account_handle.description: Canonical handle of the authenticated service account. This unsigned UX hint is only for display and local artifact naming; it MUST NOT be treated as principal identity evidence, authorization, or a service-account-to-principal binding.

account_subject.description: Stable subject for the authenticated service account. The client freezes this value from the DPoP-bound handoff and MUST require the identity-binding challenge to echo it byte-for-byte before signing.

preferred_locale.description: Optional private UI-language preference of the authenticated service account. It is returned only in this DPoP-bound handoff response so the client can continue the just-completed authentication flow in the selected language; it MUST NOT be copied into a public actor profile.

account_handoff_grant.description: Opaque, short-lived credential bound to the request DPoP key. It is not ak.session.grant and has no refresh-token semantics.

allowed_operations.description: Closed set of operations this handoff may be presented at. The abandonment command is a member because a never-accepted PCR leaves the holder without a principal, so no principal-bound ak.session.grant can carry them. The device-pairing finalize command is a member for the mirror reason: a fresh device of an already bound account has no accepted-device signer yet, so this handoff is the only sender-constrained credential that can supply the exact AccountId its target proof must sign. Membership here does not widen the handoff into a session credential.

did.description: Complete standard DID whose registered method adapter MUST project to the principal_id the Account Authority derives from principal_registration_anchor.

identity_binding_challenge_outcome.description: Only fresh challenge material and domain separation. The authority durably retains the full request, account/handoff subject, lease/fence, DID operation and independently derived pins, PCR/genesis/session digests, audience/origin/trust-domain, and rechecks all of them atomically at registration. The client reconstructs the proof from its frozen submission and authenticated onboarding context.

pcr_genesis_unit_kinds.description: Closed ordered declaration copied into the identity-root creation transcript.

identity_creation_control_proof.description: Fresh proof signed by the WebVH registration root control key. The verifier derives that key from the accepted did:webvh entry's parameters.updateKeys[0] in principal_registration_anchor and MUST NOT treat a request-supplied key or a DID Document verificationMethod as authority. proof_kind is fixed to did_webvh_inception_update_key and MUST agree with anchor_kind=webvh_registration. The Ed25519 signature covers every field except signature as canonical JSON with domain separator ak.identity_creation_control_proof.v1; signature_algorithm is part of those signed bytes.

proof_kind.description: Closed registration root-key derivation discriminator. v1 permits only did_webvh_inception_update_key paired with anchor_kind=webvh_registration.

registration_anchor_digest.description: SHA-256 over RFC 8785 JCS of the complete principal_registration_anchor. The verifier recomputes it from the submitted anchor.

pcr_realm_id.description: Principal Control Realm id obtained only by retyping the exact root-signed ak.realm.create event_id; it is not derived from principal_id and MUST equal the pcr_genesis_unit create Event's retyped id.

realm_create_payload_digest.description: Canonical digest of the ak.realm.create payload only. Event ids and envelope digests are forbidden from this transcript.

founding_authorize_payload_digest.description: Canonical digest of the founding ak.device.authorize payload only. Event ids and envelope digests are forbidden from this transcript.

initial_session_request_digest.description: SHA-256 digest of RFC 8785 JCS InitialSessionGrantRequest. The embedded session_public_key MUST thumbprint to dpop_jkt; this binds the first Standard grant intent without turning it into a separate root-signed object.

signature.description: 64-byte Ed25519 identity-root signature encoded base64url without padding.

identity_creation_control_proof.$comment: The method adapter derives the canonical pinned version/entry commitment. control_key_digest serves bounded evidence consumers, and signed method transcript positions are reconstructed from the pinned entry; caller-supplied digest mirrors are rejected.

registration_did_evidence_draft.description: Dedicated registration-time control proof and frozen method evidence. It is distinct from identity_creation_control_proof, it is a receipt rather than primary material, and it MUST bind the exact coordinates re-derived from principal_registration_anchor.

registration_anchor_control_proof_pairin.$comment: Single closed pairing between the registration anchor branch and the identity-root derivation the control proof claims. It is referenced by every carrier that ships both objects so the two members can never disagree on which adapter produced the root key.

binding_kind.description: Discriminates the already-published DID proof branch from account-first identity creation.

did.description: Verified DID whose registered adapter projects to principal_id.

did_version_id.description: Adapter-defined version identifier pinned when the account binding was accepted.

control_key_digest.description: Digest of the verified current control key that authorized this binding.

identity_creation_lease_id.description: Present only when binding_kind=identity_creation. The published_did branch creates no identity-creation lease.

registration_anchor_digest.description: SHA-256 of RFC 8785 JCS of the complete frozen typed principal_registration_anchor, including the exact method-native material of the selected branch. For binding_kind=identity_creation it is the submitted anchor; for published_did the Account Authority freezes the anchor it reconstructed from the verified method history at did_version_id. The verifier MUST recompute it from that typed object; serializing a raw JSON transport with different optional-member treatment is not equivalent.

proof.description: Account Authority detached proof. payload_digest is SHA-256 over RFC 8785 JCS of the complete receipt with proof omitted, including binding_kind, principal_id, did, did_version_id, control_key_digest, registration_anchor_digest, and the identity-creation lease/fence only when that branch applies. JWS signs canonical_json({context:'ak.account_binding_receipt_proof.v1', payload_digest, account_authority_id, account_subject, principal_id, did, did_version_id, control_key_digest, verification_method, created_at}); proof.created_at MUST equal issued_at and verification_method MUST be an assertion method of account_authority_id valid at issued_at.

propertyNames.description: ak.self.account.command.update_profile.v1 only accepts display_name, avatar_blob_ref, and profile_fields.<key>. The bio is carried as profile_fields.bio.

account_materialized_profile.description: Materialized Actor Profile returned on the account surface. id is the actor_profile ID derived by retyping the accepted ak.profile.create Event ID; realm_id is the exact Principal Control Realm that carries the profile Event lineage.

profile.description: Present only when the authenticated principal has exactly one unambiguous accepted Actor Profile across its account-local-lineage PCR lineages. Because this request has no authority selector, multiple accepted lineages MUST fail closed by omitting profile; the service MUST NOT choose an implicit current PCR.

is_server_admin.description: True when the authenticated principal is a deployment server administrator (the server's configured admin principal set). Operator-only product surfaces (e.g. organization creation) gate their UI on this. Reducer/config-derived, not a stored account field; absent or false means non-admin.

account_register_request_body.description: Canonical account binding request. Exactly one branch is required: proof binds an already-published did, while identity_creation carries the account-first DID operation and PCR genesis unit. In either branch every repeated principal_id and did in the selected proof/creation objects and genesis initial_resolution MUST equal the outer values byte-for-byte, and the Account Authority MUST independently require project(did)=principal_id before any write.

did.description: Required for both externally created and account-first identities. The server verifies the method evidence and project(did)=principal_id before persisting the PCR resolution state.

pcr_genesis_commits.description: Optional authorized disclosure of the two PCR genesis RealmCommit objects in registered unit order.

preconditions.description: This account self-service surface forbids Event preconditions. ak.profile.update concurrency is expressed only by the optional signed payload.expected_state_digest.

account_profile_event_submission.description: Holder-signed ordinary Actor Profile Event. (event.actor_id, event.station_id) MUST equal the authenticated session's exact account authority pair, and event.realm_id MUST select that pair's local unique PCR lineage. Accepted-profile presence is evaluated only within that lineage. With no accepted profile there the exact Event MUST be ak.profile.create and its materialized actor_profile ID is derived by retyping event.event_id; the create payload MUST NOT carry id. With an accepted profile there the exact Event MUST be ak.profile.update and payload.target_ref MUST equal that accepted create-derived ID. On create payload.object.principal_id MUST equal event.actor_id; on update the accepted target profile's materialized principal_id MUST equal it. Holder direct proof is required without executed_by, authorization_ref or Applet provenance. Event preconditions MUST be empty; update concurrency uses only the optional signed payload.expected_state_digest. The service submits the exact bytes through authority Event submission and MUST NOT author, rebuild, co-sign, choose an ID or add a concurrency guard. Success exists only after the current PCR governance Station atomically accepts the Event, materializes the profile result and signs its RealmCommit; exact retry returns the stored outcome and the same Commit.

account_update_profile_request_body.description: Carries exactly one holder-signed profile create-or-update Event and no unsigned profile patch.

account_update_profile_outcome.description: Stored outcome after the profile Event is authority-committed and its effect is materialized. profile.id is the create-derived ActorProfile ID, profile.realm_id is event.realm_id, and an update projects updated_by/updated_at from event.actor_id/event.created_at. commit is the exact RealmCommit covering the submitted Event. Exact Event replay returns the byte-identical stored outcome and emits no second account-aggregate delta.

account_status_record.description: Immutable Account Authority issuer-ledger record. account_status_record_id is the suite-tagged full digest of RFC 8785 JCS over every field except account_status_record_id and proof. The proof uses context ak.account_status_record_proof.v1 over that same closed unsigned core. principal_control_realm_id is a verified account-binding coordinate only and is never a finality scope.

binding_version.description: Monotonic Account Authority-local account-to-principal binding generation.

account_status_publication.description: Constrained carrier for one exact AccountStatusRecord. Initial publication carries record only; downstream fanout carries the byte-identical record plus prior receiver receipts. No receiver rebuilds or re-signs the record.

account_status_receipt.description: Receiver-signed receipt proving durable monotonic replication of one exact AccountStatusRecord. It grants no authority. proof uses context ak.account_status_replication_receipt_proof.v1 and payload_digest over RFC 8785 JCS of every field except proof.

account_status_resolve_request_body.description: Service-authenticated bounded issuer-ledger range request used for freshness checks and predecessor-gap recovery. Unauthorized or unrelated callers receive the operation's non-enumerating authority outcome.

account_status_resolve_outcome.description: Contiguous Account Authority issuer-ledger range. Records are ordered by status_seq, begin exactly at from_status_seq when present, and retain the Account Authority's original bytes and proofs.

account_status_publication_outcome.description: Durable replica operation state. accepted/duplicate are terminal for this receiver and dependency_missing performs zero writes while identifying the exact next sequence required for gap recovery.

did_binding_challenge_request_body.description: Request a single-use challenge for binding an ALREADY-PUBLISHED did to principal_id. Unlike identity_binding_challenge_request_body this carries no unpublished principal_registration_anchor and no PCR genesis digests: the DID already exists, and the Account Authority resolves did at high freshness, requires project(did)=principal_id, and never attempts to resolve did_core_id directly.

principal_id.description: Stable did_core_id to bind. It is not directly resolvable.

did.description: Already-published DID. The Account Authority MUST resolve it at the high freshness tier, require project(did)=principal_id, and MUST NOT accept caller-supplied DID history.

did_binding_challenge_outcome.description: Persisted, single-use server challenge for binding an already-published did to principal_id. The client copies every field from challenge_id through expires_at into account_registration_control_proof, adds proof_kind, request_canonical_digest and verification_method, and signs the closed proof with the current active update key of the entry pinned by did_version_id. The client MUST byte-compare principal_id, did and every other echoed field against what it expects before signing and MUST fail closed on any mismatch. request_id is idempotency metadata and is not part of the signed transcript.

account_subject.description: Service account subject that will own the binding. Signed so the proof cannot be replayed against another account.

did.description: Server-resolved did echoed into the signed proof transcript; it MUST project to principal_id.

did_version_id.description: versionId of the entry the Account Authority resolved as current; the proof MUST be signed by that entry's active update key.

witness_evidence.description: Method-native witness / freshness evidence digest resolved for this DID. Deployments that do not host the DID MUST require it: same-origin trust between registry and Station does not extend to third-party DIDs.

expires_at.description: Issued lifetime MUST be no greater than 300 seconds.

did_binding_challenge_outcome.$comment: The method adapter derives the canonical pinned version/entry commitment. control_key_digest serves bounded evidence consumers, and signed method transcript positions are reconstructed from the pinned entry; caller-supplied digest mirrors are rejected.

identity_abandonment_request_body.description: Single explicit command using a fresh holder-bound account handoff grant. The authority MUST verify a successful authentication event later than the frozen reservation creation, not merely a refreshed token. Current account, lease/fence, holder binding and never-accepted PCR are rechecked atomically. Authentication strength and cooldown remain deployment governance.

request_id.description: Idempotency identity of the abandonment. Replaying it returns the recorded terminal outcome and MUST NOT produce a second orphan-anchor tombstone.

identity_abandonment_outcome.description: Recorded terminal outcome of an explicit abandonment. One transaction recorded the orphan-anchor tombstone / audit reservation, suppressed the reserved_identity_creation checkpoint on every holder-readable surface and released the identity-creation lease. There is exactly one success terminal; every other terminal is an error reply. Whether the orphan anchor is annotated on a discovery surface, when its handle and namespace are released and how long the reservation is retained are deployment governance and are not carried here.

principal_id.description: The abandoned provisional principal. Its published entry 0 is now a permanently unusable orphan anchor: it MUST NOT be reused and continuity MUST NOT be claimed over it.

account_request_erasure_request_body.description: Record the authenticated account holder's explicit request to erase the account (ak.gate.account.command.request_erasure.v1; zh/identity/account-lifecycle.md section 8.1). The Account Authority accepts it directly on the gate surface; acceptance only records the intent and continues the Account Authority's existing erasure_pending issuance flow within the same service — it is neither the signed AccountStatusRecord nor a completion receipt. The Account Authority MUST treat this as a high-risk action and require fresh high-risk action authentication (recent login, WebAuthn, recovery key or a deployment equivalent), judged locally by the Account Authority; re-authentication strength, risk checks and cooldown are deployment governance.

request_id.description: Idempotency identity of the erasure request. Replaying it returns the recorded acceptance outcome and MUST NOT record a second intent; the same request_id with different canonical bytes is duplicate_conflict with zero writes. A different request_id while a live intent whose erasure_pending AccountStatusRecord is not yet signed exists is failed_precondition with reason_code erasure_request_already_pending.

account_request_erasure_outcome.description: Acceptance confirmation of a self-initiated account erasure request. At most one live intent record exists per account while the erasure_pending AccountStatusRecord is unsigned. This outcome proves only that the intent is durably recorded; it MUST NOT be read as record issuance or physical erasure completion. Completion is observed through the existing account-status read surface, and physical completion through the erasure receipt rail (zh/identity/account-lifecycle.md section 8).

principal_id.description: The authenticated principal whose account erasure intent was recorded.

recorded_at.description: Time the intent was durably recorded; an exact replay returns the first recording's value.

withdrawal_window_ends_at.description: Present only when the deployment grants a withdrawal window. The Account Authority MUST NOT sign the erasure_pending AccountStatusRecord before this time; once the record is signed the request is irreversible (zh/identity/account-lifecycle.md section 3 rule 3) and no withdrawal is possible.
